mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the next month reduces the discount rate applied to future earnings, lowering the present value of expected SPX cash flows and producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% over the next 30 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns turn positive in >70% of FEDFUNDS-up periods, or IC > 0.05 over a 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs coincides with stronger consumer confidence and accelerates SPX 20-day returns via higher expected corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200,000 in the current month
failure_condition: Payrolls remain below 200,000 for ≥3 consecutive months without a subsequent SPX positive 20-day return.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 250 triggers a preemptive rate cut expectation, lowering risk-free rates and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive 60-day SPX forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by 3% in the current month
failure_condition: No significant SPX return when CPIAUCSL remains below 240 for 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 signals weak manufacturing momentum, reducing growth expectations and producing negative 20-day SPX returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO stays below 105 for >6 months with SPX 20-day returns consistently positive.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in FEDFUNDS of at least 0.2% for two months create a forward-looking signal of sustained policy tightening, compressing equity discount rates and driving negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain non-negative when FEDFUNDS shows no two-month rising trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a labor market tightening that raises expected corporate profits, producing positive 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% in the current month
failure_condition: No SPX 20-day return when UNRATE remains above 3.7% for 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail sales (HOUST) above 1,200 indicates stronger consumer demand, which anticipates better earnings and supports positive 60-day SPX forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 1200 in the current month
failure_condition: No significant 60-day SPX return when HOUST remains below 1150 for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) both decline simultaneously for two consecutive months, it signals dual supply-side pressures that depress growth expectations and drive negative 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and CPIAUCSL both fall in the same month for two months in a row
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative when this dual decline pattern does not reoccur for 4 months.
